reason: The text demonstrates strong hierarchical structures that are treated as important and necessary. Joshua exercises clear leadership authority. The princes/leaders (נשיאים) have binding authority to make covenants on behalf of the congregation, and when the people complain, the leaders defend their authority and decision-making power. Most significantly, the Gibeonites are explicitly and formally assigned a subordinate hierarchical position as permanent servants (עבדים - woodcutters and water-drawers), a status that Joshua consciously establishes and validates. Hierarchy is not discouraged but rather institutionalized and maintained as essential to the social order.
